'''Józef Emanuel Jankowski''' (1790–1847) was a professor of [[philosophy]] at [[Jagiellonian University|Kraków University]].<ref>[[Władysław Tatarkiewicz]], ''Zarys...'', p. 16.</ref>

==Life==
Jankowski was [[Feliks Jaroński]]'s successor as professor of philosophy at [[Jagiellonian University|Kraków University]] from 1818 and author of a ''Logic''.<ref>[[Władysław Tatarkiewicz]], ''Zarys...'', p. 16.</ref>

Jankowski was one of nearly all the university professors of philosophy in Poland before the [[November Uprising|November 1830–31 Uprising]] who held a position that shunned both [[Positivism]] and [[Metaphysics|metaphysical]] speculation, affined to the [[Scottish School of Common Sense|Scottish philosophers]] but linked in certain respects to [[Immanuel Kant|Kant]]ian critique.<ref>[[Władysław Tatarkiewicz]], ''Zarys...'', p. 16.</ref>
